why: Each figure is a zigzag spring with one black ball at each of its two ends, whatever way the spring is turned or flipped. In figures 1, 2, 3 and 5 the balls sit exactly at the two ends of the spring. In figure 4 one ball sits in the middle of the spring, so the spring runs on past it and does not end in a ball. This breaks the rule, so figure 4 is the odd one out.
trick: Ignore rotation and flipping. Check where the small parts sit (ends or middle) and count them. The one whose position differs is the odd one.
note: Fig 3 is an upside-down (flipped) spring but still has balls at both ends; fig 4 has a ball in the middle.
